title: Boundary Value Lab — Partitions, Boundaries and Live Verdicts
description: Describe an input field's rule — an integer or decimal range, a string length, a date window or an enum — and see its equivalence partitions and boundary values on an animated number line that zooms into both edges. Switch between 2-value and 3-value boundary analysis to generate on, off and in points plus partition representatives and wrong-format cases, then type any value for a live accept or reject verdict with the reason.
prompt: Build 'Boundary Value Lab'. Let me define an input field's rules — integer or decimal ranges, string length, date windows, enums — and show the equivalence partitions and boundary values on an animated number line. Generate test cases (valid and invalid; on, off and in boundary points; 2-value and 3-value BVA) and let me try values live with a verdict. Get the edge cases right: decimal precision without floating-point surprises, real calendar dates, and string length that isn't fooled by emoji. Style it like a hazard-striped workshop tool.

methodology: Textbook oracles for BVA: for 1–10 the 3-value set must be exactly 0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 with off/on/in labels, and the 2-value set exactly 0, 1, 10, 11; the same shape is checked for decimals, lengths and dates.
Self-consistency across every field type: each generated case is clicked and its live verdict must equal the expected result printed in the table, so the generator and the validator check each other.

Domain-specific edge cases: too-precise decimals, trailing zeros, exponent notation, 29 February in a common and a leap year, day-first date formats, and emoji counted as code points rather than UTF-16 units.
Invalid rule configurations (min above max, a step finer than the limits) must produce a warning and no cases instead of nonsense.
Keyboard pass over the type tabs (Arrow keys) and a manual visual check of the broken-axis number line at 1280 and 390 px.
risks: Floating-point arithmetic producing 4999.990000001 or rejecting 0.1; all decimal work is done in integer multiples of the step.
JavaScript Date silently rolling 2027-02-29 over to 1 March; dates are round-tripped to detect it.
Huge ranges making the number line unreadable; the axis breaks between two zoomed windows.
Negative lengths appearing as off points below zero; the floor is enforced.
qa.playwright: Tests read boundary cases through data-group, data-point, data-value and data-exp attributes, so every assertion is about the data, not the formatted table. The cross-check test loops over every case on all five tabs and clicks it, so any future drift between how the generator and the validator treat a value (for example how lengths are counted) fails loudly. Date inputs are filled with ISO strings, which Playwright handles for type=date on both projects. The pin animation is ignored except for the opacity of hidden 'in' pins in 2-value mode.
coverage: Integer 3-value and 2-value sets, rule edits, min-above-max warning
Generated case equals live verdict, for all five field types
Decimal precision, trailing zeros, exponent notation, step change
String length with emoji, date window with leap years and wrong formats
Enum classes, whitespace, case-insensitive toggle, keyboard tab switching

a11y: Field types are an ARIA tab list with Arrow-key switching, every rule input is labelled, and each generated case is a button that loads the value into the labelled test input. The verdict is a polite live region with the partition and the reason in words, so the number line is supplementary.
